answer:
Set up a 2D lid-driven cavity flow simulation using OpenFOAM's icoFoam solver.
The cavity is a square with width 0.1 m and height 0.1 m, extruded in the z-direction by 0.01 m to form a single-cell-thick 2D domain.
Use a uniform Cartesian mesh of 20 cells in x, 20 cells in y, and 1 cell in z, giving a cell size of 0.005 m in x and y.
The top wall patch (movingWall) has a no-slip velocity boundary condition of fixedValue uniform (1 0 0).
The bottom, left, and right walls have no-slip velocity boundary conditions of fixedValue uniform (0 0 0).
The front and back faces have empty boundary conditions for both U and p.
The pressure boundary condition is zeroGradient on all wall patches.
The initial velocity field is uniform (0 0 0) throughout the domain.
The initial pressure field is uniform 0 throughout the domain.
The kinematic viscosity is set to nu = 0.001 m²/s in constant/transportProperties.
The time step size (deltaT) is 0.002 s.
The simulation runs from startTime = 0 to endTime = 0.5 s, totaling 250 time steps.
Results are written every 20 time steps (writeControl timeStep, writeInterval 20).
No turbulence model is applied; the flow is treated as laminar.
